cold_open.hook: AMD just hit fresh highs on AI agent hype—but the real story is Meta's Muse is eating everyone's lunch.

markets.macro_note: Breadth narrowing—mega-cap tech and AI plays running while small-caps and healthcare stumble; VIX compression suggests complacency.

big_story.story_title: Meta Muse popularity lifts AMD stock to fresh highs as AI agents juice CPU sales
big_story.angle: Meta's Muse is the first AI agent product that's actually moving hardware—not just hype—and it's reshaping the CPU market in real time; the question is whether this is a genuine shift in AI workload or just the latest cycle of 'this time is different.'

quick_hits.angle: Lambda's $4B pre-IPO raise is the largest AI compute startup funding round ever—but it's happening in a market where compute is already commoditizing; the real question is whether they're raising at peak hype or if they've actually solved a problem no one else can.
Winter heating bills are about to spike hard for millions—this is a real cost-of-living shock that doesn't show up in CPI the way it should, and it's coming right as rate cuts stall.
Emmer's 'you suck' to Senate Republicans is the kind of intra-party scorched-earth that usually signals a power vacuum or a leadership challenge brewing.

Tesla's Model 3 and Y can now act as home batteries—which sounds cool until you realize it's solving a problem most owners don't have while creating a new one: grid operators managing millions of car batteries as a distributed power plant.

odd_thing.joke_angle: A Trump rally stuck in time is just a Trump rally—the real oddity is that someone at The Atlantic thought this was news and not just a description of every Trump rally ever.

sign_off.callback_target: Meta's Muse actually moving hardware—the one AI product that isn't just a chatbot in a trench coat.
